title: Large data volumes, query selectivity, indexing, and data skew
objectives: Explain large data volume performance as reducing how many records the platform must process, using selective filters and archiving.
Define query selectivity as filters the Lightning Platform Query Optimizer can drive from indexes, and name operators that often prevent that.
Place standard, custom, Unique/External ID, and Support-requested indexes without inventing unofficial selectivity percentages.
Define ownership data skew and parent-child data skew using the 10,000-record architect thresholds, and refuse dummy-owner piles.
diagnostic_question: A report times out on 8 million LAB_ invoices, one integration user owns 200,000 of them, and 80,000 contacts sit under a dummy account. Which problem is selectivity, indexing, ownership skew, or parent-child skew—and what would you not 'fix' with a bigger timeout?
definition: Large data volume (LDV) design reduces how many records queries, reports, and sharing must touch. The Lightning Platform Query Optimizer uses indexes when filters are selective; negative and unindexed filters often force broader scans. Ownership data skew is one user owning more than 10,000 records of an object. Parent-child data skew is 10,000 or more children under one parent account, which stresses implicit sharing. ([LDV best practices](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.meta/salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp/ldv_deployments_best_practices.htm); [Ownership Data Skew](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership_data_skew.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for selective filters, indexes, and skew—not 'Salesforce is slow.' Parking unassigned leads on a dummy user or all contacts on a dummy account is the example architect docs warn about. Inventing 10% selectivity numbers you cannot cite is worse than saying the optimizer needs selective indexed filters.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a highway interchange. Selective filters are ramps only a few cars need. Indexes are HOV lanes the optimizer may use when that ramp is selective. Negative filters are 'not this exit,' which is a poor way to route traffic. Ownership skew is dumping 10,000-plus cars onto one exit (one owner). Parent-child skew is one mega-interchange (one parent account) with 10,000-plus ramps that all have to be rechecked when access changes.
deeper_explanation: LDV best practices: performance tuning relies on reducing the number of records processed. Narrow, selective queries beat broad ones. Archiving or discarding at the rate data arrives keeps volumes from degrading over time. If retrieved rows are few enough, the platform can use indexes (and other constructs such as skinny tables—request via documented channels, do not invent). ([LDV best practices](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.meta/salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp/ldv_deployments_best_practices.htm))

The Lightning Platform Query Optimizer exists because the multitenant database's native optimizer cannot always see tenant data access efficiently. It evaluates indexes against record-distribution thresholds to decide whether an index helps. Custom indexes can be requested from Salesforce Support; the platform may also auto-create indexes. Unique and External ID fields are indexed as field attributes (DQM-003) but still must be selective in the query. ([LDV infrastructure](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.meta/salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp/ldv_deployments_infrastructure_for_performance.htm))

SOQL/SOSL LDV practices: use selective filters on indexed fields with a wider range of values; avoid negative filters such as status != 'failed' or != NULL; prefer IN over huge OR lists; avoid filtering on non-deterministic / cross-object formula fields that are not indexable. Decompose OR queries that cannot use indexes. Timeouts: tune scope, consider Bulk API 2.0 query, LIMIT, or Batch Apex patterns—Needs verification of current bulk-query options in the org. ([SOQL and SOSL LDV](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp.meta/salesforce_large_data_volumes_bp/ldv_deployments_best_practices_soql_and_sosl.htm))

Ownership data skew: a single user owns more than 10,000 records of an object—common when parking unassigned leads on a dummy user. Moving that user in the role hierarchy or in/out of a sharing-rule source group forces huge sharing recalculation. Mitigations in the architect guide: distribute ownership; if you must concentrate ownership, avoid giving those users a role; if they need a role, place them in a separate top-level role and do not move them, and keep them out of public groups used as sharing-rule sources. ([Ownership Data Skew](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_group_membership_data_skew.htm))

Parent-child data skew: 10,000 or more children on one parent account (for example parking unallocated contacts under a dummy account). Implicit sharing then makes visibility changes expensive: losing access to one contact can require scanning the other children to see if account access should remain. ([Parent-Child Data Skew](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.draes.meta/draes/draes_object_relationships_parent_child_data_skew.htm))

mental_model.analogy: A highway interchange: selective filters = ramps few cars need, indexes = HOV lanes the optimizer may use, negative filters = 'not this exit,' ownership skew = 10,000-plus cars on one exit, parent-child skew = one mega-interchange with 10,000-plus ramps.
useful_mapping: object with millions of rows → a vast highway network
selective indexed WHERE → a ramp only a small slice of traffic uses
index → HOV lane the query optimizer may choose
negative filter (!=, NOT, <> ) → 'not this exit' (usually unhelpful)
ownership skew → one exit owned by one driver with 10,000-plus cars
parent-child skew → dummy account interchange with 10,000-plus child ramps
sharing recalculation → rebuilding all the signs when that driver changes roles
archive → closing old lanes so the remaining network stays small
where_it_breaks: An index is not always used; the optimizer compares distribution thresholds.
Unique/External ID indexes still fail if the filter is not selective (almost all rows match).
Lookup skew onto a popular lookup target is a sibling pattern—cite current architect docs before quoting a number.
The analogy does not encode skinny tables or exact unofficial selectivity percentages.

teach_back_prompt: Explain LDV, selectivity, indexing, and the two documented skew types with the 10,000 thresholds. Then say why a dummy account for extra contacts is dangerous. Name where the highway analogy breaks.

claims.claim: LDV performance tuning relies on reducing how many records the system must process: narrower selective queries and archiving/discarding data as new data arrives.
The Lightning Platform Query Optimizer evaluates indexes against record-distribution thresholds. Custom indexes can be requested; the optimizer will not use an index if the filter is not selective.
claims.validation: LDV infrastructure plus SOQL best practices.

claims.claim: Avoid negative SOQL filters (for example status != 'failed' or != NULL). Prefer selective indexed filters and IN lists instead of large OR chains. Avoid filtering on non-deterministic / cross-object formula fields that are not indexable.

Ownership data skew is when a single user owns more than 10,000 records of an object. Moving that user in the hierarchy or in/out of a sharing-rule source group can force long sharing recalculation. Distribute ownership; if concentrated, avoid assigning a role or isolate a top-level role and do not move it.
Parent-child data skew is 10,000 or more child records on a single parent account. Implicit sharing maintenance can require scanning remaining children when one child's access changes.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: LDV means reduce rows processed. Queries need selective indexed filters; avoid negatives. Ownership skew is one user over 10,000 rows. Parent-child skew is 10,000-plus children on one account. Dummy parking lots cause both.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from symptoms: timeout versus sharing job versus load time. Timeouts: rewrite WHERE, indexes, archive. Sharing pain after a role move: count records per owner. Contact visibility pain under one account: count children. I will not quote unofficial 10% numbers. I will not 'fix' skew with a longer timeout. Unique/External ID helps indexing but does not fix unselective filters or dummy accounts.

terminology.plain: Enough rows that unselective queries, reports, and sharing maintenance get expensive.
terminology.precise: LDV guides focus on reducing records processed via selective queries and archiving, plus platform features such as the query optimizer and indexes.
terminology.example: Tens of millions of LAB_ Invoice__c rows still queried without a date predicate.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: API daily limits, which are a different governor family.
terminology.boundary: No single official 'LDV starts at N rows' in this lesson; design for growth.

terminology.plain: Whether a filter narrows enough that an index is worth using.
terminology.precise: The optimizer evaluates distribution thresholds. Non-selective or negative filters often prevent index use even if a column is indexed.
terminology.example: WHERE LAB_Status__c = 'Open' AND CreatedDate = THIS_MONTH on an indexed status with mixed values.
terminology.non_example: WHERE Status != null on a field that is almost never null.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SOSL search crowding (also in the LDV SOQL/SOSL topic).
terminology.boundary: Quote cheat-sheet percentages only with that sheet open.

terminology.plain: A database shortcut the optimizer may use to find rows without scanning the object.
terminology.precise: Standard indexes, Unique/External ID, custom indexes (Support or auto-indexer). The optimizer still checks selectivity. Skinny tables are a related Support-mediated feature.
terminology.example: Request a custom index on LAB_InvoiceDate__c used in every timeout report.
terminology.non_example: Assuming a formula field is indexed because it is 'like a field.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Match keys in duplicate rules (DQM-003)—different feature.
terminology.boundary: Do not promise Support will always add the index.

terminology.plain: One user owns more than 10,000 records of an object.
terminology.precise: Architect guide threshold. Dummy-user parking plus role or sharing-group moves cause long sharing recalculation. Distribute owners; avoid roles on concentrated owners or isolate a top-level role you will not move.
terminology.example: Integration User owns 200,000 LAB_ invoices and is then added to a role.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Parent-child skew, which is about one parent record, not one owner.
terminology.boundary: Mass transfer onto one dummy recreates this (DQM-005).

terminology.plain: One parent account has 10,000 or more children.
terminology.precise: Dummy-account parking of contacts is the documented example. Implicit sharing can require scanning remaining children when one child's access changes.
terminology.non_example: Evenly distributed contacts under many real accounts.
terminology.boundary: Lookup skew to a popular lookup target is neighboring; cite before numbering.

terminology.plain: Salesforce's extra optimizer that picks access paths on the multitenant store.
terminology.precise: Helps produce effective queries because the native database optimizer cannot see tenant access the same way. Considers indexes, sharing filters, and statistics.
terminology.example: A report filter that finally uses an index after values become selective.
terminology.non_example: A human 'optimizing' by raising a timeout setting that does not exist here.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SQL Server/Oracle cost-based optimizer lectures that ignore sharing.
terminology.boundary: Query plan tools in the org may differ; do not invent UI clicks.

when_to_use: When interviewers ask about large data volumes, query selectivity, indexing, and data skew together.
When a report or SOQL times out and the WHERE clause uses negatives or unindexed formulas.
When one user owns more than 10,000 records and someone wants to move their role.
When more than 10,000 contacts sit under a dummy parent account.
When a team proposes parking all unassigned leads on one dummy user 'just for now.'
when_not_to_use: Do not use unofficial selectivity percentages in the interview unless you are reading the current cheat sheet.
Do not treat Unique/External ID as a cure for unselective filters or dummy-account piles.
Do not use this topic as a substitute for backup/restore (DQM-005) or migration rehearsal (DQM-007).
Do not 'fix' ownership skew by mass transferring onto a different single dummy user.
Do not quote lookup-skew numbers you cannot cite from current architect docs.
configuration_or_code_location: Object Manager: Indexed column on fields; Unique/External ID attributes.
Reports/list views/SOQL WHERE clauses; Query Plan in Developer Console if available (reverify UI).
Setup → Support cases for custom indexes / skinny tables.
Reports of record counts grouped by OwnerId and AccountId.

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox lab approximating LDV: 12,000 LAB_ invoices owned by Integration User, 11,000 LAB_ contacts under Account Unassigned, and a report that filters Invoice Status != 'Closed' on a mostly-open population.
inputs: Counts per owner and per account

decisions.decision: Rewrite the report to Status = 'Open' (or an IN of few open values) on an indexed field.
decisions.because: LDV SOQL guidance: avoid negative filters; need selective indexed predicates.

decisions.decision: Distribute invoice ownership off Integration User; do not move that user in the hierarchy while skewed.
decisions.because: Ownership skew >10,000; role moves recalculate sharing.
decisions.rejected: Adding the dummy user to a sharing-rule source group

decisions.decision: Split contacts off the dummy Unassigned account onto real or multiple holding accounts below 10k children each.
decisions.rejected: Leaving 11,000 children on one parent 'until we know'

configuration_or_code: Mass transfer slices of invoices to several owners (DQM-005) with backup.
Reparent contacts in batches; never one dummy account.
worked_example.output: Report returns; no owner or parent remains above the documented 10k examples without a written exception.
verification: Count invoices by owner; none over 10k in the lab.
Count contacts by account; Unassigned below 10k.
Report completes with the positive filter.
worked_example.self_explanation: Selectivity, ownership skew, and parent-child skew were three different piles. I did not invent a 10% number.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox. You will not create millions of rows; you will measure and design as if counts were larger.
starting_state_checks: You can run a report grouped by Owner and by Account.
steps: Create a report or SOQL that uses a negative filter; rewrite it as a positive equality/IN.
Count records by OwnerId; write whether any user would be skewed at 10,001.
Count contacts by AccountId; identify a dummy-parent risk.
List two index sources: Unique/External ID versus a Support-requested custom index.
guided_completion: If you quoted a 10% threshold, replace it with 'optimizer distribution thresholds / cheat sheet.'
If you proposed one dummy owner as the fix, stop.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Explain why moving a skewed user's role is expensive using architect-guide language.
evidence: Written 10,000 thresholds for the two skew types.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete LAB_ rows created for counts.
Do not request production skinny tables from this lab.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Sandbox row counts will not prove production optimizer choices.

decision_table.signal: Report/SOQL timeout; filter is !=, NOT, or unindexed formula.
decision_table.choose: Rewrite to selective positive filters on indexed fields; consider a custom index request.
decision_table.not: A negative filter plus 'raise the timeout.'
decision_table.why: LDV SOQL guidance: selective indexed filters; avoid negatives and non-indexable formulas.

decision_table.signal: One user owns more than 10,000 records and might change roles or groups.
decision_table.choose: Distribute ownership; if concentrated, avoid a role or isolate a top-level role you will not move.
decision_table.not: Park even more rows on that dummy user.
decision_table.why: Ownership Data Skew guide: 10k threshold and sharing recalculation on moves.

decision_table.signal: 10,000-plus contacts (or other children) under one dummy account.
decision_table.choose: Split across real parents; stop using one Unassigned account as a parking lot.
decision_table.not: Adding more children to the same parent until 'we know the account.'
decision_table.why: Parent-child skew: implicit sharing scans the sibling set.

decision_table.signal: Object grows every month and queries degrade.
decision_table.choose: Archive/discard at inflow rate; keep hot queries narrow.
decision_table.not: Only adding more reports on the full history.
decision_table.why: LDV best practices: reduce records processed; archive as data arrives.

decision_table.signal: Need an index on a frequently filtered custom field that is not Unique.
decision_table.choose: Work with Salesforce Support (and check auto-indexer); still require selective values.
decision_table.not: Marking the field External ID 'for indexing' without an integration key.
decision_table.why: Indexes are Support/auto or field attributes; External ID is for outside identifiers (DQM-003) and still needs selectivity.

limitations: Does not fully specify skinny tables.
Does not design the entire sharing model.
Lookup skew needs a current citation before numbers.
security_notes: Skewed dummy users with roles can accidentally inherit broad access if placed high in the hierarchy.
Do not copy production extracts into this lab.
Sharing recalculation is a security-maintenance cost, not just a performance footnote.
common_mistakes: Quoting unofficial 10% selectivity as gospel without the cheat sheet.
Parking leads on a dummy user with a role.
Parking contacts on a dummy account.
Assuming any indexed field makes every filter fast.
Using != NULL as a selective filter.

troubleshooting.symptom: Report times out after the object grew.
check: Whether an index exists and values are selective.
Whether the report is really a full-table scan of history.

troubleshooting.symptom: Sharing recalculation runs for hours after a role change.
check: Records owned by that user (10k+ skew).
Whether they are in sharing-rule source groups.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: Apex is the cause by default.

troubleshooting.symptom: Account access changes are slow when a contact is removed.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The contact trigger is always the bottleneck.

production_notes: Design owners and parents before the first million rows.
Request indexes with evidence (slow queries, fields, operators).
This lesson does not authorize production skinny-table or index cases without architect review.

mcqs.prompt: Main LDV performance approach in the best-practices guide?

options.A: Reduce the number of records the system must process

mcqs.rationale: LDV BP: reduce records processed via selective queries and archiving.

mcqs.prompt: Ownership data skew threshold in the architect guide?

options.A: A single user owns more than 10,000 records of an object
options.B: A user owns more than 25 External IDs

mcqs.rationale: Ownership Data Skew: more than 10,000 records of an object.

distractor_explanations.D: Roles are relevant to mitigation, not the definition.

options.A: 10,000 or more child records on a single parent account

mcqs.rationale: Parent-Child Data Skew: 10,000 or more children with a single parent account.

mcqs.prompt: Which filter style does the LDV SOQL guidance tell you to avoid?

options.A: Negative filters such as status != 'failed' or != NULL
options.B: Equality on an indexed selective field
options.C: IN lists of a few Ids
options.D: Filtering on Name instead of split First/Last where advised

mcqs.rationale: Avoid negative filters; they are called out explicitly.

distractor_explanations.C: IN is preferred over huge OR lists.
distractor_explanations.D: The guide actually suggests Name when filtering first+last.

mcqs.prompt: Why might an indexed field still not speed a query?

options.A: The optimizer uses indexes only when the filter is selective relative to distribution thresholds
options.B: Indexes never work on custom fields
options.D: External ID fields cannot be indexed

mcqs.rationale: Infrastructure: optimizer evaluates indexes against record-distribution thresholds. SOQL: if filters aren't selective, optimizer doesn't use indexed columns.

distractor_explanations.C: Sharing filters are considered; they do not globally disable indexes.
distractor_explanations.D: External ID is an indexed attribute.

mcqs.prompt: Dummy user owns most leads and is then moved in the role hierarchy. Risk?

options.A: Long-running sharing recalculation from ownership data skew
options.B: Automatic hard delete of the leads

mcqs.rationale: Ownership skew guide: moving such users in the hierarchy adjusts a very large number of sharing entries.

mcqs.prompt: If concentrated ownership is unavoidable, the architect guide suggests?

options.A: Do not assign those users a role, or isolate a top-level role you will not move and keep them out of sharing-rule source groups
options.B: Give them every role in the hierarchy
options.C: Put them in every public group

mcqs.rationale: Mitigation bullets in Ownership Data Skew.

distractor_explanations.C: Guide says keep them out of those groups.

mcqs.prompt: Why is parking 300,000 contacts under one dummy account dangerous?

options.A: Parent-child skew: implicit sharing may scan remaining children when access to one contact changes

mcqs.rationale: Parent-Child Data Skew uses this exact parking-lot story.

distractor_explanations.B: Contacts often require accounts—that is why people park them.

mcqs.prompt: Who evaluates whether an index will make a query faster?
mcqs.rationale: LDV infrastructure: query optimizer evaluates each index against distribution thresholds.

mcqs.prompt: Filtering on a non-deterministic cross-object formula field?

options.A: Avoid; those formula fields are not indexable per LDV SOQL guidance
options.D: The only way to get sharing

mcqs.rationale: Avoid cross-object reference formula fields; they aren't indexable.

options.A: Owner-centric 10k+ on one user vs child-centric 10k+ on one parent account

mcqs.rationale: Two DRAES topics, two shapes, both use 10,000 as the documented warning level.

mcqs.prompt: Best first response to 'just raise the timeout' on an unselective LDV report?

options.A: Tune the query: reduce scope, selective indexed filters, archive; consider Bulk query patterns if still needed
options.B: Agree that timeouts are the official LDV feature
options.C: Mass transfer all rows to one user

mcqs.rationale: LDV SOQL: tune, reduce scope, selective filters; mentions LIMIT and Bulk API 2.0 query if still timing out.

interview_questions.question: What does Salesforce mean by large data volumes in this topic?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Enough rows that you must reduce records processed: selective indexed queries, archiving, and avoiding skew. It is a design problem, not a vibe that 'the cloud is slow.'
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote LDV best practices: reduce scope, archive as data arrives, let indexes work when filters are selective. I add the query optimizer because multitenant statistics differ from a single-tenant DBA story. I do not invent a row number where LDV 'starts.' I separate API limits from LDV query cost.
interview_questions.example: Millions of invoices still reported without a date predicate.
tradeoffs: Keep all history hot vs archive
Custom index vs rewrite the report
follow_ups: Where does Bulk API 2.0 query fit?

interview_questions.question: Explain query selectivity and indexing without unofficial percentages.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The optimizer uses an index when the filter is selective enough versus data distribution. Indexed plus unselective still scans. Avoid negatives and non-indexable formulas. Custom indexes come from Support or auto-indexer.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk a bad filter: Status != null. I walk a better one: Status = 'Open' AND a date range on indexed fields. Unique/External ID fields are indexed but can still be unselective if almost every row matches. I point interviewers to the cheat sheet for numeric thresholds instead of guessing 10%. I mention IN versus giant OR.
follow_ups: Will OR of two indexed fields always use indexes?
weak_answer_warnings: Reciting a 10% rule as if it were in this handbook page

interview_questions.question: All unassigned leads go to Dummy User, who has a role. What do architect docs say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That is ownership data skew once they own more than 10,000 leads. Moving Dummy User in the hierarchy or sharing groups can force huge sharing recalculation. Distribute owners or isolate the user per the guide.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I tell the parking-lot story from the guide. I refuse 'just for now' if the pile will grow. If they must concentrate, I repeat: no role, or a top-level role you will not move, and stay out of sharing-rule source groups. Mass transfer onto another dummy is not a fix (DQM-005). Quality owners still matter (DQM-004).
interview_questions.example: 200,000 LAB_ leads on Integration User who then joins a regional role.
follow_ups: Partner account ownership note in the same article?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling dummy-user parking a best practice

interview_questions.question: Marketing dumps 80,000 contacts on Account Unassigned. Why do architects care?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Parent-child data skew: 10,000-plus children on one account. Implicit sharing can scan the other children when one contact's access changes. Split the pile.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the mailing-list example from Parent-Child Data Skew. Convenience of a required AccountId is how orgs get here. I plan multiple holding accounts or real accounts, loaded in batches, with backup (DQM-005). I do not promise lookup-skew numbers I cannot cite. I mention loads onto a skewed parent can also be slow.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Unassigned account with 80,000 contacts; user loses one contact and account sharing maintenance crawls.
tradeoffs: Many holding accounts vs data model change
follow_ups: Is 10,000 a hard platform error or a performance warning?
weak_answer_warnings: Leaving them on one parent until cleanup 'someday'

interview_questions.question: When would you request a custom index?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When production queries/reports repeatedly filter a field with selective values and the field is not already indexed, and rewriting the filter is not enough. Support (or auto-indexer) creates it. Selectivity still required.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I gather evidence: object size, filter operators, approximate distinct values, timeouts. I do not mark External ID on a random field 'for the index' if it is not an outside key (DQM-003, 25-field budget). I avoid formula-field filters. I mention skinny tables only as a Support-mediated LDV feature, not a DIY Setup click.
interview_questions.example: LAB_InvoiceDate__c on every timeout report; request custom index after confirming the date predicate is selective.
weak_answer_warnings: External ID on every column for speed

interview_questions.question: A sharing recalculation exploded after a small role change. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Count records owned by users in that role. If someone owns 10k+, you hit ownership skew. Check public groups used as sharing-rule sources. Do not start by rewriting Apex.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pull owner counts, group membership, and whether the user was moved into/out of a source group. I read the architect mitigation list. Short-term: stop moving them. Medium-term: distribute ownership with mass transfer to many real users (backup first). I keep parent-child skew as a separate check if Account access is the symptom instead.
interview_questions.example: Dummy User with 80,000 accounts moved from No Role into a mid-hierarchy role.
tradeoffs: Freeze hierarchy changes vs redistribute now
follow_ups: How do you find the top owners?
Does Private OWD make this worse or better?

interview_questions.question: A DBA says 'just add indexes like Oracle.' How do you Salesforce-correct them?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: We have a platform query optimizer, tenant statistics, sharing filters, and Support-mediated custom indexes. Selectivity still matters. Sharing and skew are first-class, not afterthoughts.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I respect their cost-based intuition, then I add multitenant facts from LDV infrastructure. I forbid negative filters as 'not equals is fine.' I add ownership and parent-child skew because the slow operation might not be the SELECT—it might be sharing maintenance. I will not promise we can CREATE INDEX on Friday afternoon in Setup.
interview_questions.example: Oracle DBA wants an index on a formula; LDV says those filters are not indexable.
tradeoffs: DBA muscle memory vs platform rules
weak_answer_warnings: Pretending Salesforce has no optimizer story

interview_questions.question: Highway-interchange analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Selective ramps, HOV indexes, not-this-exit negatives, 10k cars on one owner exit, 10k ramps on one dummy-account interchange. It breaks because an HOV lane (index) is not always used if the ramp is not selective.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map archive to closing old lanes. I map role moves to rebuilding every sign on the skewed exit. I break it: lookup skew needs its own citation; cheat-sheet percentages are not painted on the highway; skinny tables are a special road the platform builds, not a paint job. I refuse dummy parking lots.
interview_questions.example: Teaching why != Closed is a bad ramp on a mostly-open highway.
tradeoffs: Distribute traffic vs isolate one exit
